critical_code_review_comments: Fix is minimal and targeted: inline style={pointerEvents:'auto'} on the outer overlay of QuickGuideModal + CloseConfirmDialog correctly overrides the body-level pointer-events:none that Radix Dialog primitive sets on document.body. This is the right override — clean and localized.

Note (observation, not a bug): During test cycles I saw the note count fluctuate (4 -> 3 -> 4) when Escape was pressed multiple times in rapid succession. It self-recovered. Not related to this fix; possibly an unrelated debounce/optimistic-update quirk worth watching in future testing.

rca of the issue: iter_51 RCA (now FIXED): Radix Dialog primitive sets document.body { pointer-events: none } while open (its own overlay re-enables clicks inside the dialog). QuickGuideModal was rendered as a sibling React child (not through Radix Dialog primitive), so the body's pointer-events:none cascaded to it, killing real mouse clicks. Fix in this iteration: inline style={pointerEvents:'auto'} on the outer overlay div of QuickGuideModal AND CloseConfirmDialog explicitly re-enables pointer events on that subtree, overriding the inherited body style. Verified fix works in all 7 modal contexts including the harshest nested-dialog case (Settings > Backup > QuickGuide).
